subject: Clarify default storage horizon for debug traces vs persisted artifacts
messages:
From: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@brightbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Legal Ops <legal-ops@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: how long do you keep developer traces vs persisted outputs?

Hi Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks for the call this morning. BrightBank's security team asked for a very specific clarification for our contract: we need to know the default "storage horizon" for two different classes of artifacts when using Redwood's hosted API.

1) Developer/debug traces (request/response headers, tokenization traces, streaming fragments, KV-cache snapshots used only for debugging).
2) Persisted artifacts (final generated outputs that might be indexed, embeddings, and evaluation records).

Can you confirm the default retention windows for both categories (hosted, and if different, for eu-hosted), and explain what counts as a developer trace versus a persisted artifact? Also, what the erase/attestation path looks like (how we demonstrate deletion to auditors).

We may need language for procurement and a short bulleted table for our legal team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sarah
Product Security, BrightBank
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: how long do you keep developer traces vs persisted outputs?

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the follow-up and apologies for the rapid-fire notes on the call. High level answer first, then a concise table we can drop into procurement: 

- Developer/debug traces: default 30 days on hosted (US), 30 days on EU regions by default. These include full request/response bodies when the customer has not opted into "no-store" or "private mode", streaming fragment buffers for in-flight retries (kept transiently), and ephemeral KV-cache snapshots stored only to support live inference.

- Persisted artifacts: default 365 days for customer-visible artifacts created by customers (embeddings, indexable outputs, eval logs). Customers can request shorter retention or deletion. For Private deployments/VPC, retention follows customer-managed settings.

Audit/evidence path: we generate a deletion attestation with timestamps and object ids; for hosted customers we can provide a signed proof of deletion that references the internal object keys and purge job run id. We also keep immutable audit logs of the purge event (SLA: 48 hours to produce evidence).

I pushed a small matrix to Drive (link below) and attached the draft spreadsheet — happy to iterate.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: can you add official language about what we consider "developer trace" in legal-speak?
- Marissa: please confirm EU region defaults and whether any customers in pilot have a different baseline.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@brightbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: how long do you keep developer traces vs persisted outputs?

Sarah, Jordan —

High-level legal definition and proposed procurement-friendly copy below. I've tried to keep it short for contract exhibits. Let me know if you want anything hardened for BrightBank's SOC/audit language.

Definition (proposed):
- "Developer trace": non-production artifacts created to support inference lifecycle and debugging. Examples: raw request payloads captured for troubleshooting, tokenization traces, streaming buffer fragments, intermediate KV cache snapshots, and transient logs that are not surfaced as customer artifacts. Developer traces are retained by default for 30 days in all hosted regions unless the customer opts into a no-store configuration.
- "Persisted artifact": any model-generated content or derivative that the customer elects to store or that is produced as part of a customer-visible product flow (final generative outputs, embeddings, index snapshots, exported eval datasets). Persisted artifacts are retained by default for 365 days for hosted customers; customers may configure shorter retention or request deletion at any time.

Procurement exhibit language (short):
"Redwood will retain debugging artifacts (developer traces) for a default period of 30 days and customer-visible persisted artifacts for a default period of 365 days. Customers may request deletion of any stored artifact; Redwood will provide proof of deletion within 48 hours of request for hosted accounts. For Private or Dedicated deployments, retention is controlled by the customer's configuration and the applicable service agreement."

Attachments: I attached a simple matrix (redwood_default_storage_matrix_v1.xlsx) with edge cases (streamed fragments, kv-cache, embeddings).

If that looks good I can convert to an exhibit and send to BrightBank legal.

-Kim
Head of Compliance Documentation, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, BrightBank Legal Ops <legal-ops@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: how long do you keep developer traces vs persisted outputs?

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifying bullets from our legal team after reviewing the matrix: 

- For streaming fragments: confirm they are never written to cold storage unless there is an active debug capture (customer-triggered) — your wording suggests transient buffer only but legal prefers explicit statement.
- For KV-cache snapshots: confirm those are ephemeral and excluded from "persisted artifacts" unless the customer explicitly exports them.
- Deletion proof: BrightBank requests that the attestation include the object id prefix plus the purge job run id and the hash of the purge manifest. That is standard for our auditors.

If you can add those bullets to the exhibit I'll route to procurement. Also confirm that the 48-hour SLA is for evidence production and not necessarily completion of background purge processing (we understand purge may run on a schedule).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — once we have the exhibit we'll insert into the SOW.

—Sarah
Product Security, BrightBank
